paper_metadata.title: A Zr-45Ti-54Al-3V alloy with excellent elevated temperature mechanical properties: Millimeter-scale coarse grains with initial subgrains
paper_metadata.journal: International Journal of Refractory Metals and Hard Materials

evidence.quote: a Zr-45Ti-54Al-3V alloy with initial subgrains microstructure and millimeter-scale coarse grains is prepared herein via an electric field-assisted high-temperature compression process
a new room temperature high strength alloy with the nominal composition of Zr – 45Ti – 5Al – 3V(wt%, 47Zr) have been developed by Liang et al.
The alloy without EFHC treatment is called as-forged alloy, otherwise it is called EFHC-treated alloy.
After the EFHC treatment at 1200 °C, the α-phase is seen to have grown into a lamellar form with a width about 127 nm
When the EFHC treatment temperature is increased to 1400 °C, the α-phase is seen to have broadened to 243 nm, and a new α” phase is observed (Fig. 11).
The alloy was melted three times using a vacuum consumable electro-arc furnace to ensure a uniform chemical composition.
The ingot underwent multiple breakdowns after being held at 1050 °C above the β transit temperature for 1.5 h to completely break the coarse grain.
The ingot was then held at 930 °C for 1.5 h.
The final heat forging was performed, and the ingot was lathed into bars 43 mm in diameter.
Finally, the EFHC treatment was performed at the target temperature under a uniaxial pressure of 10 MPa for 10 min.
